<fragment>

*Mongolian Mark* won the Yi Sang Literary Award. The rest of the series (*The Vegetarian* and *Fire Tree*) were delayed by contractual problems.[5] Han was the youngest to receive Yi Sang Literary Award in 2005[18] until 2013 when Kim Aeran received it at the age of 32. Her *Human Acts Archived 2018-04-28 at the Wayback Machine* was released in January 2016 from Portobello Books.[19] Han has been chosen to win the Malaparte Prize 2017 with the Italian translation of *Human Acts*, "*Atti Umani"* from Adelphi Edizioni, 2017 in Italy on 1 October 2017.[20][21]


Han Kang's 2017 autobiographical novel *The White Book* centers on the loss of her older sister, a baby who died two hours after her birth.[7] In 2018 Kang became the fifth writer chosen to contribute to the Future Library project.


In 2023, she published her fourth full-length novel, *Greek Lessons*. The Atlantic called it a book in which "words are both insufficient and too powerful to tame."[22]

The rest of the series (*The Vegetarian* and *Fire Tree*) were delayed by contractual problems.[5] Han was the youngest to receive Yi Sang Literary Award in 2005[18] until 2013 when Kim Aeran received it at the age of 32. Han Kang's 2017 autobiographical novel *The White Book* centers on the loss of her older sister, a baby who died two hours after her birth.[7] In 2018 Kang became the fifth writer chosen to contribute to the Future Library project.
